# Quality-scale research

Researched 7 November 2026 against primary Home Assistant documentation and the aiohomekit 4.0.1 sources. This is a gap inventory from the initial local implementation, not a certification or a statement that subsequent implementation work passed. No Home Assistant instance, real HomePod, controller credential, backup, keychain, remote repository or publication was accessed or changed for this research.

## What “Platinum” means here

The official scale is cumulative: Bronze has 20 rules, Silver adds 10, Gold adds 21 and Platinum adds 3. Meeting the three Platinum rules alone is insufficient. The [official rule inventory](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/rules/) and [tier-raising procedure](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/raise-tier/) require all applicable rules through the target tier. A `quality_scale.yaml` claim uses `done`, `todo`, or `exempt`; an exemption needs a specific justification. [Quality-scale file reference](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/quality-scale-file/).

For this custom integration, a manifest entry cannot award an official tier: Home Assistant 2026.11.0's `Integration.quality_scale` returns `custom` for integrations outside core, even if their manifests contain `quality_scale: platinum`. Keep the public description **custom integration with local quality gates** until there is independently supported evidence for stronger wording. A local checklist can use the official rules as engineering targets. Passing that checklist does not imply Home Assistant acceptance, HACS/Marketplace acceptance, supported hardware verification or published release validation. [Owning loader implementation](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.11.0/homeassistant/loader.py#L907-L912).

The requested **100% statements and branches** is a repository gate stricter than the official Silver coverage requirement of **more than 95% per module**. Bronze separately requires full config-flow coverage. Synthetic coverage cannot establish successful extraction of real credentials or real-device behavior. [Silver coverage rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/test-coverage/), [config-flow coverage rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/config-flow-test-coverage/).

## Complete rule inventory and local evidence routes

The rule identifiers and grouping below follow the [official inventory](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/rules/). Each identifier links to its owning rule. The last column is a local observation or proposed verification, not an official rule quotation. `Review` means an implementation exists but needs evidence before a `done` claim. `Todo` means a concrete initial gap. `External` means local tests alone cannot close it. `Exemption candidate` must retain its stated scope and be reviewed.

## Dependency and typing conclusions

aiohomekit 4.0.1 describes itself as an asyncio client. Its tagged packaging configuration includes `aiohomekit/py.typed`, and its source exposes useful typed classes. That is evidence of PEP 561 support, not proof that every API has strict annotations: for example the inherited controller initializer and several networking methods have missing annotations, while pairing payloads use `dict[str, Any]`. Verify the marker in the actual installed wheel and run the intended checker against the exact versions used in validation. [Tagged packaging](https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/blob/4.0.1/pyproject.toml), [IP controller](https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/blob/4.0.1/aiohomekit/controller/ip/controller.py), [zeroconf controller](https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/blob/4.0.1/aiohomekit/zeroconf.py).

`IpController` inherits `ZeroconfController(char_cache, zeroconf_instance)`. This code already passes HA's `AsyncZeroconf`; there is no aiohttp/HTTPX session parameter to inject. `HomeKitConnection` opens sockets with `aiohappyeyeballs` and an asyncio transport; its protocol implements HAP framing, encryption and events itself. The library's own explanation says conventional HTTP clients cannot supply its required security/event behavior. HAP has HTTP-like messages, so the precise claim is **custom encrypted HAP socket transport with no conventional HTTP session**, not “HomeKit has no HTTP syntax.” [Controller constructor](https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/blob/4.0.1/aiohomekit/zeroconf.py#L185-L191), [socket implementation](https://github.com/Jc2k/aiohomekit/blob/4.0.1/aiohomekit/controller/ip/connection.py), [library explanation](https://pypi.org/project/aiohomekit/4.0.1/).

The web-session rule expressly permits raw-socket protocol exceptions. A reasoned exemption for this HAP implementation is defensible and should remain visible for review; passing an unused HA session into an adapter would prove nothing. Reassess if a conventional outbound HTTP client is introduced. Inbound HA import views and the browser's same-origin upload do not create an outbound Python HTTP-session dependency. [Web-session rule and exceptions](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/inject-websession/).

The async dependency rule concerns device/service network I/O, not a ban on using an executor for protected disk I/O. Audit synchronous filesystem calls before marking it done, particularly setup, journal validation, persistence and removal. [Async dependency rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/async-dependency/).

Strict typing has no general exemption. The equivalent custom-repository gate should run strict mypy over **every** packaged integration Python module, using the supported Python version and installed HA/aiohomekit versions. Define `type HomePodConfigEntry = ConfigEntry[Runtime]`, a typed coordinator data contract and small validated record/payload models. Use accurate dependency-facing protocols or narrowly justified casts at untyped boundaries; do not hide the integration behind `Any`, `ignore_errors`, blanket `ignore_missing_imports`, disabled strictness, or an excluded module list. The official `.strict-typing` registry belongs to core; creating a similarly named local file alone does not enable type checking. [Strict typing rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/strict-typing/).

aiohomekit's PyPI page supplies release files and provenance metadata, and its tagged project declares Apache-2.0. Preserve the tag/artifact/provenance evidence when assessing dependency transparency; an invented release-workflow URL is not evidence. Review other direct imports too. [PyPI release and provenance](https://pypi.org/project/aiohomekit/4.0.1/), [dependency transparency rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/dependency-transparency/).

## Implementation decisions that require care

**Actions.** Register both administrator actions during `async_setup`, once. Keep their definitions available when the entry fails or unloads. A handler should find the current singleton entry and validate that it is loaded before accessing `runtime_data`; otherwise raise a translated `ServiceValidationError`. Operational failures should become a translated `HomeAssistantError`, with controlled placeholders that cannot expose keys or addresses. Exercise actions before any loaded entry, after unload and after a successful reload. [Action setup](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/action-setup/), [setup/action exception guidance](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/integrations/setup-failures/).

**Reauthentication.** This integration authenticates with controller identities; therefore the “no authentication” exemption is false. Introduce an actual `async_step_reauth` route bound to the existing entry and local administrator identity. Reuse the bounded private import path, validate the same accessory/controller pins, and update/reload the existing entry without copying secrets into `entry.data`. Never treat reauthentication as permission to overwrite a changed pinned identity or reset persisted recovery limits. A multi-device entry needs deliberate per-device handling: one credential problem must not silently discard healthy devices. Raise/start reauth on actionable confirmed credential failure, while transient network failures retain retry semantics and identity mismatches retain fail-closed behavior. [Reauthentication rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/reauthentication-flow/).

**Translations and repairs.** Remove hardcoded measurement names to use fitting device-class translations, or supply valid entity translation keys. Status needs a key, finite state labels and `icons.json` mapping. Keep custom integration `translations/en.json` synchronized with the canonical strings, including action, exception and issue strings. Repairs should tell users what they can do for persisted credential/permission failure, corrupt protected state, or competing-engine conflict; a passing transient outage is not automatically an actionable repair. Associate issues with the config entry and clear them when resolved or a device is removed. Ordinary unload must not discard the user's ignored issue state. Persistent notifications alone do not implement the Repairs rule. [Entity names](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/entity-translations/), [exception translations](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/exception-translations/), [icon mappings](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/icon-translations/), [repair lifecycle](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/repair-issues/).

**Dynamic and stale devices.** This is a multi-device entry. Neither rule's single-fixed-device exemption describes it. A discovered unselected HomePod must never be automatically commissioned: credentials and pairing changes still require explicit authorization. Once an additional device has been explicitly prepared and approved, however, runtime/entity listeners can publish its records without reloading all healthy devices. If the design deliberately retains reload-only additions, record dynamic-devices as `todo` or an explicitly reviewed custom scope exception, not the official fixed-device exemption. Keep listener cleanup and remove/re-add deduplication in the test plan. [Dynamic devices](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/dynamic-devices/).

For stale devices, mDNS disappearance does not prove deletion. The official rule allows user removal when the integration cannot know authoritatively. Existing `async_remove_config_entry_device` is a useful implementation route: test it for loaded and unloaded entries, storage failures, foreign registry records, owned entities and retained native entities/history. An offline HomePod is not grounds to erase its credential or cooldown history automatically. [Stale devices](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/stale-devices/).

**Discovery changes.** Test fresh resolution of a known pinned accessory after IP/port changes. The stable accessory identity must remain the trust anchor. The singleton's domain-wide flow unique ID can prevent duplicates but is not itself a per-accessory identity match; the existing read-time backend resolution may satisfy the runtime behavior, provided tests establish it. [Discovery update rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/discovery-update-info/).

## Evidence gates and truthful exceptions

Local quality work can establish exact full coverage, a failing-on-error strict typing command, lint/format checks, action/flow/repair/translation contracts and reproducible offline HA compatibility tests. At inspection, `devtools/coverage-baseline.json` still permitted misses and `scripts/validate.sh` did not invoke a strict type checker. Re-run the final commands after implementation; this research does not record a passing result.

Keep these external deliverables open until there is separately approved evidence:

- **Maintainer and distribution identity:** real codeowner consent, project-owned HTTPS documentation, issue/private security reporting routes and authenticated source history. The current manifest points at native HomeKit documentation, which is not this custom project's own guide. The [manifest reference](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/integrations/manifest/) requires custom documentation to point to its own HTTPS documentation.
- **Brand acceptance and official tier:** the official brands rule requires upstream assets and has no ordinary exemption; local artwork and tests cannot prove accepted upstream branding. A future core submission/tier review is a separate external action. [Brands rule](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/quality-scale/brands/).
- **Real hardware/firmware and credential extraction:** observe the authorized extraction route, first setup, stable readings, administrator recovery, restart and removal on supported devices before claiming tested compatibility. Document failures and limits without credentials. This is a project release/support gate; do not misrepresent it as an automatic implication of coverage or an externally passed certification.
- **Hosted validation and released artifact:** hosted CI, tag/archive contents, distribution acceptance, published documentation and installation are independent outcomes. Local checks are evidence only of local checks.

Legitimate exemption candidates are narrowly scoped: no custom conditions; no custom triggers; and the custom encrypted HAP socket transport for web-session injection. Reauthentication, strict typing, brands, multi-device dynamic behavior and actionable Repairs must not be exempted merely because they are difficult, external, safety-sensitive or unfinished. A local policy departure should remain a clearly explained `todo`/external gate unless the actual official exception fits.
